correction: Three beliefs from the retired 2026-07 sysext were wrong. (1) The upstream `curl | sh` installer was thought to do the NSS/PAM wiring; it only adds the APT repo, installs packages, writes domain/options into /etc/himmelblau/himmelblau.conf and runs `systemctl enable --now` -- the deb maintainer scripts do all of the /etc integration (nss-himmelblau.postinst sed on nsswitch.conf; pam-himmelblau.postinst runs pam-auth-update, appends the krb5 includedir and adds use_authtok to gdm-password), and in a sysext build those run only in the chroot against the delta's /etc, which never ships. (2) [retracted the same day, see the next entry] a 7-second container probe suggested himmelblaud 4.0.2 runs with no domain configured; it does not. (3) Writing /etc/himmelblau/himmelblau.conf was assumed harmless; himmelblau.conf(5) parses only the highest-priority MAIN file, so an /etc main file masks the deb's /usr/lib/himmelblau/himmelblau.conf and the Debian-required defaults in it (local_groups, home_attr/home_alias, use_etc_skel) -- which is exactly why the upstream installer re-emits those lines. snosi writes a conf.d drop-in instead. Also: Trixie's apparmor package keeps the unix-chkpwd profile in complain mode, so himmelblau-apparmor's patch is moot there, and Trixie's krb5-user no longer creates /etc/krb5.conf.
evidence: Installer source https://himmelblau-idm.org/install (build_install_plan: steps apt_prereqs, apt_repo, install_packages, write_global_config, note 'Community packages configure PAM/NSS integration during package installation', enable_services); /var/lib/dpkg/info/{nss,pam}-himmelblau*.postinst on the enrolled Ubuntu 26.04 host 10.0.1.174; Trixie container: himmelblaud 4.0.2-debian13 stayed alive 7s as a non-root user with no domain -- too short, it exits at ~13s; himmelblau.conf.5 CONFIGURATION PRECEDENCE section; /etc/apparmor.d/unix-chkpwd in debian:trixie apparmor 4.x = flags=(complain); after `apt install krb5-user` in the container /etc/krb5.conf did not exist.
